summary: SSE early-ack from edge proxy leads to lossy choice reassembly on resumed streams
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteFlow Labs reports that after transient network blips through their corporate load balancer, resumed SSE streams occasionally drop the last N tokens of a partial 'choice' and do not reassemble subsequent continuation fragments. The pattern looks like the edge LB sends an early TCP ACK or application-layer ACK which causes the downstream proxy to consider a chunk delivered and not forward a trailing continuation chunk on the resumed connection.

Impact:
- Affects long streaming responses (3+ second generations) behind some enterprise LBs/proxies.
- Customers see truncated sentences at the end of a choice and occasionally duplicate leading tokens on the resumed chunk.
- Reported by a single dedicated-customer workspace so far, but similar symptoms seen in internal synthetic tests.

Environment:
- Customer: dedicated stack in us-east-1 behind corporate LB (F5 variant).
- Redwood components: edge API gateway -> streaming-proxy -> serving-runtime (gRPC internal).
- Models: redwood-v1-13b with streaming SSE endpoint and choice chunking enabled.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a long streaming request that produces multi-second responses (e.g., long-form summarization).
2) Trigger a short network interruption between client and corporate LB (simulate client-side reconnect).
3) Client reconnects and calls SSE resume using existing session ID; LB immediately returns ACK for previously sent segments.
4) Observe resumed stream: terminal choice sometimes missing trailing words; occasionally a small duplicate token at resume boundary.

Observed behavior:
- Missing trailing words in the terminal choice (incomplete final sentence).
- Inconsistent reassembly: sometimes the continuation chunk arrives but is dropped by the proxy as already-acked.

Expected behavior:
- Resumed SSE should stitch continuation fragments correctly; no loss of final tokens and no duplication.

investigation_notes: Proxy behavior: streaming-proxy marks chunk boundary complete on receipt of full application chunk. However, edge proxy interaction with LB fast-ACK can trigger a state where trailing fragment metadata is considered acknowledged though not forwarded on reconnection.
gRPC/serving-runtime logs: serving-runtime received continuation fragments in all runs; issue occurs between streaming-proxy and client-facing gateway/LB layer.

Hypothesis: LB early ACK causes the client-facing gateway to drop retransmission of last fragment; streaming-proxy's resume logic trusts gateway ACK state and does not request missing fragment, leading to silent loss.
Repro script: added test harness that simulates TCP ACK-only behavior; reproduces 80% of observed truncations when aggressive ACK enabled.
Relevant metrics: increased 'stream-resume-mismatch' counters in staging when proxy ack-trust toggled. Added a temporary gauge to track 'resume-missing-fragments'.
Related PRs under consideration: streaming-proxy change to re-verify fragment sequence on resume (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/427).
resolution:
In progress - workaround and planned fix:
Workaround: customer-side: add a 200-500ms delay before issuing resume or switch to websocket fallback for sessions behind known aggressive LBs. Support has communicated this and customer reported reduced truncations.
Planned fix: change streaming-proxy resume path to re-request or validate last sequence id from serving-runtime when an ACK race is detected. Patch PR #427 created and currently in review. After QA in staging we will roll out a hotfix to prod with a feature-flag guard and slow rollout across regions. Post-deploy, monitor 'resume-missing-fragments' gauge and customer feedback.
Follow-ups: 1) Add diagnostic flag in API to log resume sequence mismatch for easier customer debugging. 2) Update troubleshooting runbook and add a KB article describing LB knob compatibility.
